criteria.evidence: Natural-language Arabic; no formal symbolic alphabet or WFF grammar. L1 letter-layer test was a negative finding (letters carry no recoverable structure).
A single dominant generative core exists, but no explicit axiom list and recovering 80% of structure needs 57% of concepts (F2: proto-axiomatic, residue 0.901).
No stated inference rules; none are formalised in the text.
No proof calculus (no Hilbert / natural-deduction / sequent structure).

Derivation-LIKE structure is real and validated: the L6 network predicts a verse's content from related verses at 0.545 vs random 0.325 (p=0.005); rare-content 0.20 vs 0.019. But this is semantic entailment, not formal proof.
F1: global consistency 0.95, 0 surviving genuine contradictions across 6832 relations.
Numerics layer: 0 of 499 well-posed tests survive Bonferroni/FDR (min p=0.0057); number-blind protocol. No robust arithmetic structure -> Gödel's theorems do not apply.

verdict: NOT A FORMAL SYSTEM (in the mathematical-logic sense). The Quran MEETS consistency (strong) and shows real, validated derivation-LIKE semantic structure, but lacks a formal language, explicit inference rules, and a proof calculus, and has no arithmetic encoding. Correct classification: a CONSISTENT, PROTO-FORMAL semantic system with a coherent generative core — the same class the author's own audit assigned to the book (Proto-Formal Axiomatic System). The word 'formal' in the author's claim is an over-statement; 'consistent and axiom-structured' is accurate.
